info.title: DEMS Core API
info.summary: Core API v1 of the DEMS Edge Client demo, as the Core server answers it: 97 operations and one WebSocket channel.
info.description:
Reference for the Core API v1 of the **DEMS Edge Client demo** (device DEMS-IR-01), as the **Core server** answers it. The design book (§21.2) names nine endpoints; this document adds their bodies, and the operations both clients need beyond them: sign-in, user administration, pairing, the session lifecycle, evidence, devices, storage, network and time, security and audit, system, alerts and the demo controls.

### Who answers

| Service | Address | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| The Core server (`dems-core-server`) | `http://127.0.0.1:4420` | Every operation of this document and `WS /ws`. It keeps the Core state in PostgreSQL and is the only authority on who may do what. Loopback only. |
| mock-core (`dems-mock-core`) | `http://127.0.0.1:4400` | `GET /api/v1/health` and a heartbeat-only `WS /ws`. It is the service of Simulated mode and answers no other operation. |
| The in-app simulator | none | In Simulated mode, the nine design-book operations (`x-dems-mode: simulated`), inside the app and without a request. Its answers carry `x-dems-simulated: 1`; the Core server never sends that header. |

Every operation carries the badge **LIVE**: the Core server answers it over the network. `x-dems-services` names the services that answer an operation, and `x-dems-mode` says whether the in-app simulator can answer it too (`simulated`) or only a service can (`live`).

### Access

The Core server decides on every request, before the body is read, from the credential the request carries:
- a **web console** sends the session cookie that `signIn` set (scheme `sessionCookie`);
- a **paired device** sends `Authorization: Bearer` (scheme `bearerAuth`): its device credential on the device operations and at sign-in, its session token once an operator is signed in.

A request carries one credential, never both. Each operation states its access rule as `x-dems-access` (PUBLIC, DEVICE, AUTHENTICATED, one permission, or the one any-of) and the audit row it writes as `x-dems-audit`. A refusal for a missing permission answers `403` and writes one audit row; the role and its permissions are read from the database for each request.

### Answers every operation shares

The answers that do not depend on the operation are defined once, under Responses: a malformed path, an unknown route, a wrong method, a server that is not ready, an Origin outside the allowed lists, two credentials in one request, the request throttle, a body over 65,536 bytes, and an unexpected failure. Every answer carries `x-request-id`, and an error repeats it as `error.requestId`. A 2xx answer of a POST carries `x-dems-epoch` and `x-dems-revision`: the state revision that holds the effect of the command.

### Lists

A list is cursor-paged: `cursor` is the `nextCursor` of the page before, `limit` is 1 to 200 (50 when omitted), and `nextCursor` is null on the last page.

### Not part of this API

- Media and evidence package files are not served: the clients keep their bundled demo media, and the server owns the records, the hashes and the verdicts.
- No operation creates or deletes a user, changes a password or edits the role matrix.
- No operation takes a file or resolves a path that a client sent.

### Examples

Examples are frozen at 2026-10-01 10:00:00 WIB and follow the canonical demo dataset: session SES-20261001-0024 (case LP/2026/1001-0007) and evidence EV-20260930-0004, exported by the SUPERVISOR operator. The nine design-book operations write times as ISO-8601 text; every other operation writes epoch milliseconds on the server clock. A password, a pairing code, a session token, a device credential and a biometric token appear only as placeholders that open nothing. All data is synthetic.

tags.name: Service
tags.description: Liveness of the service that answers: the Core server, or mock-core in Simulated mode. Public; it returns nothing of the Core state.

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Sign-in, the caller's own auth session, and biometric sign-in on a paired device. The server is the only authority: a web console holds its session in an `HttpOnly` cookie, a paired device sends a bearer value. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Administration
tags.description: The role and permission matrix (read-only) and user administration: assign a role, enable, disable. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Pairing
tags.description: One-time pairing codes and the registry of paired devices. A device pairs by entering a code that a Supervisor issued. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Session
tags.description: Session lifecycle (book §6.2): CREATE → PRECHECK → ARMED → RECORDING → STOPPING → FINALIZING → SEALED, with FAULT and RECOVERY after a critical fault. One session is open per Core. The commands need SESSION_START; markers, notes and snapshots need SESSION_NOTE; every role reads the open session and the history. Answered by the Core server; in Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the four design-book operations.

tags.name: Device
tags.description: The devices of the Core (book §6.1, §21.2): health, audio channels, video tracks, the inventory and the device commands. AUDIO-01 and AUDIO-02 are reported separately in every answer. Answered by the Core server; in Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the three design-book reads.

tags.name: Storage
tags.description: Evidence storage: capacity, state, history and the retention policy. Answered by the Core server; in Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the design-book status read.

tags.name: Evidence
tags.description: Evidence items with their tracks, hashes, custody chain and verification, and the authorized export with chain of custody (book §19.2, §19.3). No operation changes a sealed item, and none serves a media file. Answered by the Core server; in Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the design-book export.

tags.name: Network
tags.description: The network of the Core device and its time service: simulated hardware signals, read-only. The time service is not the server clock, which stamps every record. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Security
tags.description: The security status, the audit log and its hash chain, the audit and log exports, and the operational events. Every signed-in role reads; the two exports need AUDIT_EXPORT. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: System
tags.description: The Core device, its services, diagnostics, the simulated software update and the display preferences. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: The alerts of the Core and their acknowledgement. Every alert was raised by a fault, and raising it wrote a FAULT_RAISED audit row. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Demo
tags.description: Scenarios, fault injection and the reset to the seed state, behind DEMO_CONTROL and the server-side demo flag. Answered by the Core server.

tags.description:
WebSocket `/ws`. OpenAPI 3.1 cannot describe a socket, so it is documented here. Two services serve it:

| Service | URL | Sends |
|---|---|---|
| The Core server (`dems-core-server`) | `ws://127.0.0.1:4420/ws` | The protocol of the section "Core server": `hello`, the heartbeat, the replicated Core state, the audio meters and the control messages |
| mock-core (`dems-mock-core`) | `ws://127.0.0.1:4400/ws` | The heartbeat only (section "mock-core"): the socket of Simulated mode |

### Core server

The Core server serves `ws://127.0.0.1:4420/ws` with the protocol below. A lane instance serves the same path on its own port.

**Who a connection is.** Decided once, at the upgrade, from the request headers only: the session cookie of a web console, or `Authorization: Bearer` of a paired device. Nothing in the URL, in a subprotocol or in a message authenticates. The principal stays for the life of the connection, so a client opens a new socket after a sign-in or a sign-out.

| Principal | Receives |
|---|---|
| ANONYMOUS | `hello`, `heartbeat` |
| DEVICE | `hello`, `heartbeat`, `device.revoked` |
| OPERATOR | `hello`, `heartbeat`, `snapshot`, `delta`, `meters`, `session.updated`, `session.ended`, `device.revoked`, `admin.changed` |

**Server to client.** One JSON object per text frame; every message carries `type` and `v: 1`.

| `type` | Topic | Members | Model | Sent to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hello` | none | `connectionId`, `epoch`, `principal`, `reason?`, `topics`, `serverTime`, `heartbeatIntervalMs` | RealtimeHello | Every connection, first. |
| `heartbeat` | heartbeat | `seq`, `serverTime`, `uptimeMs`, `intervalMs`, `clients`, `sessionState` | Heartbeat | Every connection, once a second. `sessionState` is null unless the principal is OPERATOR. |
| `snapshot` | state | `epoch`, `revision`, `serverTime`, `state` | RealtimeSnapshot | OPERATOR: after `hello`, as the answer to `resync`, and when a new epoch starts. |
| `delta` | state | `epoch`, `revision`, `serverTime`, `ops` | RealtimeDelta | OPERATOR, for every change of a replicated slice. |
| `meters` | meters | `at`, `seq`, `audio` | RealtimeMeters | OPERATOR, after `subscribe`. |
| `session.updated` | control | `operator` (`id`, `role`), `permissions`, `reason` | RealtimeSessionUpdated | The sockets of the operator's sessions. |
| `session.ended` | control | `reason` | RealtimeSessionEnded | The sockets of the session, which are then closed with 4401. |
| `device.revoked` | control | `reason` | RealtimeDeviceRevoked | The sockets of the device, signed in or not, which are then closed with 4403. |
| `admin.changed` | admin | `resource` | RealtimeAdminChanged | OPERATOR holding USER_ADMIN (`USERS`) or PAIRING_MANAGE (`DEVICES`, `PAIRING_CODE`). |

**Client to server.** Anything else, or a message from a principal that may not send it, closes the connection with 1008.

| `type` | Members | Allowed for | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subscribe` | `topic: meters` | OPERATOR | The server starts the `meters` frames. |
| `unsubscribe` | `topic: meters` | OPERATOR | The server stops them. |
| `resync` | none | OPERATOR | The server answers with a new `snapshot`. At most one in 2 s; one that comes sooner is answered when the 2 s have passed. |

**State.** After `hello` an OPERATOR connection gets one `snapshot` with the 30 replicated slices (the ReplicatedState model). Every later change is a `delta` whose `revision` is the previous one plus 1 within the `epoch`: revisions have no gap, and a state delta is never dropped. A delta holds operations: `replace` carries one whole slice, `append` carries new rows of `audit` (with `head`, `total` and `dropped`) or of `events`. A slice that no operation names did not change. A client that sees a gap, or another epoch, sends `resync` (at most one in 2 s) and gets a new `snapshot`. A demo reset, a scenario load and a server start begin a new epoch. A 2xx answer of a POST carries the same two numbers in `x-dems-epoch` and `x-dems-revision`, so a client knows which delta holds the effect of its command. Not replicated: `clock`, `auth`, `authLockout`, `pairing`, `audio`. The audio frames travel in `meters` only; a client builds the other four itself, from the server time and from the answers of the identity and pairing operations.

**Time.** `heartbeat.serverTime` is an ISO-8601 string, as mock-core writes it too. Every other time of the protocol is epoch milliseconds on the server clock.

**Close codes.**

| Code | When | What a client does |
|--:|---|---|
| 1001 | Server shutdown. | Reconnect with the backoff. |
| 1008 | Protocol violation: an unknown message, one the principal may not send, or too many. | Reconnect. |
| 1009 | A client message larger than 65,536 bytes; the socket library refuses it before it is buffered. | Reconnect. |
| 1013 | The connection cap is reached. | Reconnect later. |
| 4401 | The session ended (any reason of `session.ended`), or the bearer value is not valid. | Show the login screen. A web console opens an anonymous socket for the heartbeat. |
| 4403 | The device was revoked or unpaired. | Delete the device credential and show the pairing screen. |
| 4408 | The client did not read fast enough; no state delta is dropped instead. | Reconnect and resynchronise. |

**Never in a message.** A password, a session token, a cookie value, a device credential, a biometric token, a pairing code or a QR payload, or any hash or salt of those; the `enabled` flag or the session list of another operator; the list of paired devices; the lockout state of another console. `admin.changed` names the list that changed and holds no row of it.

**Examples.**

`hello` to a signed-in investigator:

```json
{
  "type": "hello",
  "v": 1,
  "connectionId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a1",
  "epoch": 3,
  "principal": "OPERATOR",
  "topics": [
    "heartbeat",
    "control",
    "state",
    "meters"
  ],
  "serverTime": 1790823600000,
  "heartbeatIntervalMs": 1000
}
```

`hello` to a connection whose cookie no longer resolves to a session:

```json
{
  "type": "hello",
  "v": 1,
  "connectionId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a5",
  "epoch": 3,
  "principal": "ANONYMOUS",
  "reason": "SESSION_INVALID",
  "topics": [
    "heartbeat"
  ],
  "serverTime": 1790823600000,
  "heartbeatIntervalMs": 1000
}
```

`delta`:

```json
{
  "type": "delta",
  "v": 1,
  "epoch": 3,
  "revision": 129,
  "serverTime": 1790823600000,
  "ops": [
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "slice": "tabletLink",
      "value": {
        "state": "CONNECTED",
        "changedAt": 1790823600000
      }
    },
    {
      "op": "append",
      "slice": "events",
      "rows": [
        {
          "id": "LOG-000061",
          "seq": 61,
          "at": 1790823600000,
          "type": "TABLET_CONNECTED",
          "severity": "INFO",
          "message": "Tablet connected",
          "params": {
            "state": "CONNECTED"
          },
          "sessionId": "SES-20261001-0024",
          "deviceId": "TABLET"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`meters`:

```json
{
  "type": "meters",
  "v": 1,
  "at": 1790823600000,
  "seq": 22440,
  "audio": {
    "inputs": {
      "MIC-01": {
        "seq": 22440,
        "at": 1790823600000,
        "dbfs": -18.4,
        "peak": -12.1,
        "clip": false,
        "noSignal": false
      },
      "MIC-02": {
        "seq": 22440,
        "at": 1790823600000,
        "dbfs": -51.7,
        "peak": -50.9,
        "clip": false,
        "noSignal": false
      }
    },
    "activeInputId": "MIC-01"
  }
}
```

`session.updated`:

```json
{
  "type": "session.updated",
  "v": 1,
  "operator": {
    "id": "OPR-001",
    "role": "TECHNICIAN"
  },
  "permissions": [
    "EVIDENCE_VIEW",
    "DEVICE_MANAGE",
    "DIAGNOSTICS_RUN",
    "MAINTENANCE",
    "CAPTURE_CONFIG"
  ],
  "reason": "ROLE_CHANGED"
}
```

`session.ended`:

```json
{
  "type": "session.ended",
  "v": 1,
  "reason": "TOKEN_REUSE"
}
```

`device.revoked`:

```json
{
  "type": "device.revoked",
  "v": 1,
  "reason": "REVOKED"
}
```

`admin.changed`:

```json
{
  "type": "admin.changed",
  "v": 1,
  "resource": "USERS"
}
```

`subscribe`, sent by a client:

```json
{
  "type": "subscribe",
  "topic": "meters"
}
```

`resync`, sent by a client:

```json
{
  "type": "resync"
}
```

### mock-core

- Server to client only: one JSON `Heartbeat` message (see the Heartbeat model) per text frame every 1000 ms, plus one immediately after connecting.
- `seq` counts ticks since the server started. `sessionState` is `null` in this demo phase.
- Upgrades from origins other than the web dev origins and the service's own origins are refused with 403.
- Clients show the link as STALE after 2500 ms without a heartbeat and reconnect after 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s (the last delay repeats), plus up to 250 ms of jitter.
- Messages sent by clients are ignored.

Example message:

```json
{
  "type": "heartbeat",
  "v": 1,
  "seq": 5400,
  "serverTime": "2026-10-01T03:00:00.000Z",
  "uptimeMs": 5400012,
  "intervalMs": 1000,
  "clients": 2,
  "sessionState": null
}
```

Liveness of the service that answers. Public: it needs no credential and returns nothing of the Core state.

- The Core server answers `service: dems-core-server` with its version and `ready`, which says whether its database and its engine are ready. The status is `200` for as long as the process answers, so a stopped database shows as `ready.database: false`.
- mock-core, the heartbeat-only service of Simulated mode, answers `service: dems-mock-core` and no `ready`.

This is not the device health snapshot; that is `GET /api/v1/device/health`.

post.description:
Creates a session and returns its Session ID; the session enters **CREATE** (book §6.2, §12.2 steps 1-2).

Idempotent (S26): the same input while that session is still open returns it with `200` and `created: false`.

Requires a signed-in operator holding SESSION_START; writes the SESSION_CREATED audit row.

One session is open per Core, and any operator holding SESSION_START may act on it. A caller whose role lacks the permission is refused with `403 NOT_PERMITTED` and one ACCESS_DENIED audit row, before the body is read.

The Core server's refusal texts are fixed and quote no part of the request: a session that is not the open one answers `404 NOT_FOUND` "This session is not the open session." (`details.simCode: NOT_FOUND`), and an action that does not fit the session's state answers `409 INVALID_STATE` "The action is not allowed in the current state." with `details.simCode: ILLEGAL_STATE`, `from` and `event`. A `409 SESSION_ACTIVE` names the open session in `details.sessionId`. The examples show the texts of the in-app simulator.

Answered by the Core server. In Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the same operation inside the app, without a request, and marks its answer with the header `x-dems-simulated: 1`; the Core server never sends that header.

post.description:
Runs the Core pre-check (book §5.3: 8 checks) and starts recording.

- From **CREATE**: begins the pre-check and answers `202` with state **PRECHECK**. Poll `GET /api/v1/session/current` and call again once it is **ARMED**.
- From **ARMED**: starts recording and answers `200` with state **RECORDING**.
- Pre-check ended with **WARN**: send `{"acknowledgeWarnings": true}` to acknowledge and start; without it the answer is `409 PRECHECK_WARNINGS`.
- Pre-check with a **BLOCK** (Core offline, lens fault, storage full, security fault): `409 PRECHECK_BLOCKED` with the reasons.

Requires a signed-in operator holding SESSION_START; the audit rows name that operator.

One session is open per Core, and any operator holding SESSION_START may act on it. A caller whose role lacks the permission is refused with `403 NOT_PERMITTED` and one ACCESS_DENIED audit row, before the body is read.

In a real capture operation a start is refused `503 NOT_READY` with `details.reason: CAPTURE_HELPERS_LEFT` while helper processes of an earlier capture are still running (envelope level; nothing is opened twice).

A body that does not match its schema answers `422 INVALID_INPUT`. The pre-check and its outcome also have operations of their own: `beginPrecheck`, `retryPrecheck` and `acknowledgePrecheckWarnings`.

The Core server's refusal texts are fixed and quote no part of the request: a session that is not the open one answers `404 NOT_FOUND` "This session is not the open session." (`details.simCode: NOT_FOUND`), and an action that does not fit the session's state answers `409 INVALID_STATE` "The action is not allowed in the current state." with `details.simCode: ILLEGAL_STATE`, `from` and `event`. A `409 SESSION_ACTIVE` names the open session in `details.sessionId`. The examples show the texts of the in-app simulator.

Answered by the Core server. In Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the same operation inside the app, without a request, and marks its answer with the header `x-dems-simulated: 1`; the Core server never sends that header.

post.description:
Stops the recording with a mandatory reason and moves the session to finalization: **STOPPING** → **FINALIZING** (hashes, manifest, encryption, signature) → **SEALED** (book §6.2, §12.2 steps 5-10).

Answers `202` at STOPPING; poll `GET /api/v1/session/current` for the seal.

Requires a signed-in operator holding SESSION_START; the RECORDING_STOPPED row names that operator.

One session is open per Core, and any operator holding SESSION_START may act on it. A caller whose role lacks the permission is refused with `403 NOT_PERMITTED` and one ACCESS_DENIED audit row, before the body is read.

A stop while the recording is still connecting its cameras (`captureDurable: false`: nothing durable is written yet) is refused `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: CAPTURE_NOT_DURABLE`; nothing is changed.

The operator who stops a recording need not be the one who started it. A reason that is absent, or shorter than 5 characters after trimming, answers `422 INVALID_REASON` after the `404` and the `409`; a reason that is not text, holds U+0000 or an unpaired surrogate, or is longer than its maximum, and a malformed `{id}`, answer `422 INVALID_INPUT`.

The Core server's refusal texts are fixed and quote no part of the request: a session that is not the open one answers `404 NOT_FOUND` "This session is not the open session." (`details.simCode: NOT_FOUND`), and an action that does not fit the session's state answers `409 INVALID_STATE` "The action is not allowed in the current state." with `details.simCode: ILLEGAL_STATE`, `from` and `event`. A `409 SESSION_ACTIVE` names the open session in `details.sessionId`. The examples show the texts of the in-app simulator.

Answered by the Core server. In Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the same operation inside the app, without a request, and marks its answer with the header `x-dems-simulated: 1`; the Core server never sends that header.

post.description:
**RBAC + audit required** (book §19.3, §21.2). The Core server applies the role of the operator whose session the request carries, before the body is read.

- SUPERVISOR (holds EVIDENCE_EXPORT): `202`, and an EVIDENCE_EXPORTED audit row (the ExportEvent).
- INVESTIGATOR or TECHNICIAN: `403 FORBIDDEN`, and an EXPORT_DENIED audit row (EVT-26).

Only SEALED, UNDER_REVIEW or EXPORTED evidence can be exported, and the sealed source is never modified (book §19.3 rule 1).

The answer holds no file: the server records the export, and a client keeps its bundled export archive (01_specs §11). The reason is mandatory. A reason longer than 500 UTF-16 code units, a destination longer than 120, and any other body that does not match its schema, answers `422 INVALID_INPUT`; the server does not cut a text.

A refused export is still recorded: the EXPORT_DENIED row is committed and reaches every client through the `state` topic. The `403` carries no `x-dems-epoch` or `x-dems-revision` header (API-7 names the 2xx answers only).

REAL evidence is case-scoped (SEC35-16; review finding R93-02): a caller with EVIDENCE_EXPORT who neither holds the case nor is a SUPERVISOR is refused `403 NOT_PERMITTED` with `details.reason: EVIDENCE_CASE_SCOPE`, with one ACCESS_DENIED row.

Answered by the Core server. In Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the same operation inside the app, without a request, and marks its answer with the header `x-dems-simulated: 1`; the Core server never sends that header.

post.description:
Creates an auth session from a username and a password. It is accepted from exactly two kinds of caller (ID-1):

- a **web console**: the request carries a web console `Origin` and no `Authorization` header. The session is delivered only as an `HttpOnly` cookie; the body holds no token.
- a **paired device**: the request carries the device credential as `Authorization: Bearer`. The session token is returned once in `sessionToken` and is bound to that device; no cookie is set.

Any other caller gets `403 DEVICE_NOT_PAIRED`: pairing is mandatory for everything that is not a web console.

An unknown username, a wrong password and a disabled operator give the same `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, with `details.attemptsRemaining`. Every attempt writes exactly one audit row: AUTH_SUCCESS, AUTH_FAILED or AUTH_LOCKED. A valid session presented with the request is ended (rotation, ID-6).

The body or the answer holds a secret. It is never logged, and the API Reference offers no "Try it" for this operation in Live mode.

Core server only: the in-app simulator has no such operation, so it is not available in Simulated mode.

post.summary: Sign in with the biometric token
post.description:
Creates a session from the token that the device's biometric prompt released (§5.6). The server never accepts a claim that a biometric check passed; it accepts only the token, sent with the device credential.

The request must present the device credential itself. The session token of an operator who is signed in on this device is refused with `403 DEVICE_NOT_PAIRED` (`details.reason: DEVICE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`): a session that is still open must not be able to renew itself with a token.

Each use rotates the token: the answer carries the next one in `biometricToken`. A token that was already used, or a live one presented by another paired device, revokes its whole family, ends the open biometric sessions of that device and operator, and answers the generic `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS`.

Every attempt counts toward the device's lockout and writes one audit row: AUTH_SUCCESS (`details.method: BIOMETRIC`), AUTH_FAILED or AUTH_LOCKED.

The body or the answer holds a secret. It is never logged, and the API Reference offers no "Try it" for this operation in Live mode.

Core server only: the in-app simulator has no such operation, so it is not available in Simulated mode.

post.description:
Returns a short-lived signed URL to the NM-11 media route, which serves the decrypted camera file with HTTP Range support (M8). The route is registry-external like `/ws`; it carries its own static rule and its token prefix `mts_` joins both log-blanking lists (SEC35-13; E-31; check M8-BLK-1).

The URL is a bearer value (SEC35-12): HMAC-signed with the SEPARATE media-session signing key (`MEDIA_SESSION_SIGNING_KEY_ID`, never the evidence Signer key), bound to one `(operatorId, sessionId, evidenceId, fileId)` and rejected if any component differs, alive for exactly `EVIDENCE_MEDIA_SESSION_TTL_MS`. It never enters a log, an audit row or a replicated slice (E-31).

LIVE only: Simulated mode plays the bundled demo media and opens no media session (NM-11; MS-1 stays true for Simulated mode). No playable decrypted file answers `409 MEDIA_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

Request (ruling D140): an OPTIONAL body `{ fileId: VIDEO-01 | VIDEO-02 }`; no body or `{}` plays `VIDEO-01`. Refusals of this operation: `403 NOT_PERMITTED` with `details.reason: EVIDENCE_CASE_SCOPE` (REAL evidence of a case the caller does not hold; one ACCESS_DENIED row); `409 MEDIA_NOT_AVAILABLE`, for a package that cannot be played with `details.reason` one of `NOT_A_SEALED_PACKAGE`, `PACKAGE_MISSING`, `MANIFEST_UNREADABLE`, `MANIFEST_NOT_OF_ITEM`, `CAMERA_FILE_MISSING`, `CAMERA_FILE_SIZE_MISMATCH`, `FRAGMENT_TABLE_INVALID`, `FRAGMENT_TOO_LARGE`, `SESSION_KEY_UNAVAILABLE`, `FRAGMENT_NOT_AUTHENTIC`; `503 NOT_READY` (`details.reason: CREDENTIAL_STORE_NOT_READY`) at envelope level. The media route itself (registry-external, `GET /media/{token}`) refuses with `403 NOT_PERMITTED` and `details.reason: MEDIA_SESSION_INVALID` (not a token of this Core, an altered one, or one bound to another operator or session; one ACCESS_DENIED row) or `MEDIA_SESSION_EXPIRED` (an authentic token past its lifetime; no row - ask operation 88 again).

Writes EVIDENCE_MEDIA_SERVED: fileId, bytesServed, the optional range markers, signed, expiresAt — never the URL and never a byte of media (`C3 §5.2`). For REAL evidence the caller must additionally own the case/session or be a SUPERVISOR once SEC35-16 is confirmed (provisional; M8).

Core server only: the in-app simulator has no such operation, so it is not available in Simulated mode.

Stores the `{ username, secret }` pair for the camera in the path, encrypted at rest (`dbc-3 §B.3`). Needs CAPTURE_CONFIG (SUPERVISOR, TECHNICIAN — D4 OD-10) and is idle-only (`409 CAPTURE_CONFIG_LOCKED`, no audit row — SEC35-19).

**Web console only** (`C3 §3.1`, erratum PE-121-05; D80(3)): the condition `WEB_CONSOLE_SESSION` refuses a session of a tablet or a phone with `403 NOT_PERMITTED`, `details.reason: WEB_CONSOLE_ONLY` and one ACCESS_DENIED row, before the body is used. `{id}` is always a registered capture device: a candidate of a camera search is adopted with operation 96, which stores its credential in the same transaction. Both fields are printable ASCII. On the Core server the answer is `503 NOT_READY` with `details.reason: CREDENTIAL_STORE_NOT_READY` while the Core credential store is not available; nothing is stored then.

**Write-only** (RK-12; specs C-N8; M2-CRD-1): the answer is the plain `CaptureConfig` snapshot and never echoes either field; no slice, log line or audit row carries the username, the secret, the ciphertext, the nonce or the key; no operation returns a credential. The CAPTURE_CREDENTIAL_SET row names `deviceId` (and the optional operationId/permission) only (`C3 §5.2`).

Reading the store belongs to the single owning module and the audited supervisor reveal path (`dbc-3 §B.3/§D`; SEC35-02; the CAPTURE_CREDENTIAL_REVEALED row carries `deviceId` and a SCREAMING_SNAKE reason, never the value).

post.description:
Stores a change of the STT configuration. Needs CAPTURE_CONFIG — SUPERVISOR and TECHNICIAN hold it (the permission of the device selector). The body names `revision` (the optimistic lock) and the members to change.

**Accepted while a session is open, applied to the next one.** The open session keeps the snapshot taken at its start; the answer carries `appliesFrom: NEXT_SESSION` (and `pendingForNextSession: true`). When idle the answer carries `appliesFrom: NOW`.

**The credential is write-only** (E-30/E-31; SEC35-14): no answer, slice, log line or audit row carries the credential, its reference target, a ciphertext or a nonce. An answer says only whether one is set (`credentialSet`) and how it is held (`credentialKind`).

**A body that carries `credential` is web console only** (S99-09; the rule of `WEB_CONSOLE_SESSION` on operations 89, 95 and 96): a session of a tablet or a phone that sends the member - `SECRET`, `REFERENCE` or `CLEAR` - is refused `403 NOT_PERMITTED` with `details.reason: WEB_CONSOLE_ONLY` and one ACCESS_DENIED row, before the credential is read, sealed or stored. The same session may send every other member: a change without `credential` is not refused for the console.

On success writes one STT_CONFIG_CHANGED row whose details are exactly `changedFields` (the changed field NAMES, comma-joined; never a value), `enabled`, `backend`, `credentialChanged` and `revision`. An update that changes nothing writes no row and keeps the revision. No row on a refusal.

Refusals: a stale `revision` answers `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: REVISION_CONFLICT`; a value outside the contract answers `422 INVALID_INPUT` with `details.reason` `ENDPOINT_NOT_LOOPBACK` (OD-13: loopback only), `LANGUAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED` or `BACKEND_UNKNOWN`. On the Core server a `SECRET` credential answers `503 NOT_READY` (`details.reason: CREDENTIAL_STORE_NOT_READY`) while the Core credential store is not mounted. The in-app simulator has no credential store to wait for: it accepts a `SECRET` opaquely, keeps nothing of it and answers `credentialKind: ENCRYPTED` (as it does for the camera credential of operation 89).

A change of the backend, the endpoint, the model or the credential forgets `lastTest`: the last test tested another configuration.

Simulated: the in-app simulator emulates this operation (OD-17 supersedes the old "simulator untouched" rule, OD-23); in Simulated mode a client calls it inside its own simulator.

post.description:
Starts one camera search: an unauthenticated WS-Discovery probe on the network of the Core, for a fixed listening window. **No body.** No address, subnet, interface, port, timeout or filter can be sent: a search always probes the fixed multicast group. It opens no connection to any device, authenticates nothing and registers nothing.

Needs CAPTURE_CONFIG (SUPERVISOR, TECHNICIAN), on the web console, a tablet or a phone. Answers `202` with the new search; `200` with the same object and `created: false` when the caller's own search is still RUNNING (no second probe). The candidates are read with operation 94, by the session that started the search and by no other.

A search is allowed while a session is open. While that session is in `RECORDING` it is allowed only because `CAPTURE_DISCOVERY_DURING_RECORDING_ENABLED` is true (D86 C-4); with the constant off the answer is `409 INVALID_STATE` (`DISCOVERY_NOT_ALLOWED_WHILE_RECORDING`): 0 datagrams, no audit row, no alert. Another operator session's running search answers `409 INVALID_STATE` (`DISCOVERY_IN_PROGRESS`): one socket per Core. Never `409 CAPTURE_CONFIG_LOCKED`.

Writes one CAPTURE_DISCOVERY_SEARCHED row when the window closes or the search fails: the search id, the trigger, the outcome and four counts, never an address or a device text. A search with no responder writes that one row and raises one WARNING alert (`SYSTEM`, `params.reason: CAPTURE_DISCOVERY_EMPTY`); the next search with a responder resolves it.

Over a bound the Core server answers `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `retry-after` and `details.reason` `DISCOVERY_RATE_LIMITED`: nothing is sent and no audit row is written. `503 NOT_READY` carries `details.reason` `DISCOVERY_NOT_READY` when no discovery adapter is provided or capture is not ready. Both are envelope-level answers of the contract.

Simulated: the in-app simulator emulates this operation (OD-17 supersedes the old "simulator untouched" rule, OD-23); in Simulated mode a client calls it inside its own simulator. The simulator opens no socket and waits on no timer: it answers `202` with a search that is already COMPLETE (`windowMs: 0`) and two fixed candidates.

post.summary: Test the connection to a candidate camera
post.description:
One read-only connection attempt against the candidate in the path, inside one time limit: authenticate, list the media profiles, look for a usable H.264 profile. It changes no setting of the camera and is never repeated without a new operator action.

**Web console only.** Needs CAPTURE_CONFIG and a web console session (`WEB_CONSOLE_SESSION`): a session of a tablet or a phone is refused `403 NOT_PERMITTED` with `details.reason: WEB_CONSOLE_ONLY` and one ACCESS_DENIED row, before the body is used. Idle only: with a session open it answers `409 CAPTURE_CONFIG_LOCKED` and writes no audit row.

**The target is the candidate in the path and nothing else** (R-9 AC-10): the Core takes the address from its own search state. A foreign id, an expired id and a candidate that is not testable are refused with 0 outbound requests.

`credential` is required for a `PRODUCTION` candidate (`422 INVALID_INPUT`, `details.reason: CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`): no credential means no connection attempt. A `DEVELOPMENT` candidate (a fixture on loopback) may be tested without one. Both fields are 1 or more printable ASCII characters. **The credential is write-only and lives for this one request** (C-N15; SEC35-34): it is not kept in the candidate state, not cached for a later request, and never written to a log line, an audit row, an error or a file. A retry is a new request with a newly sent credential.

**A failed test is a `200` result, not an HTTP error.** Exactly five outcomes: `REACHABLE`, `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`, `WRONG_PROFILE`, `NOT_H264`, `UNREACHABLE`. The answer holds no device error text, no URL and no credential member. Every accepted attempt writes one CAPTURE_CONNECTION_TESTED row, whatever the outcome: ids, the outcome and facts, never the username, the secret or a URL (`host` and `endpointRef` for a PRODUCTION candidate only).

Other refusals, each before any request leaves the Core: `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason` `CANDIDATE_ALREADY_REGISTERED` (plus `details.deviceId`), `CANDIDATE_NOT_TESTABLE` or `CONNECTION_TEST_IN_PROGRESS`.

Over a bound the Core server answers `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `retry-after` and `details.reason` `CONNECTION_TEST_RATE_LIMITED` or `CONNECTION_TEST_LOCKOUT_GUARD` (too many refused credentials on this host): nothing is sent and no audit row is written. `503 NOT_READY` carries `details.reason` `DISCOVERY_NOT_READY`. Both are envelope-level answers of the contract.

Simulated: the in-app simulator emulates this operation (OD-17 supersedes the old "simulator untouched" rule, OD-23); in Simulated mode a client calls it inside its own simulator. The simulator contacts nothing: the first fixed candidate answers `REACHABLE`, and the body is accepted opaquely, never stored and never echoed. On a tablet or phone the simulator refuses with the same `403`.

post.description:
Registers the candidate in the path as a capture device. **This is the one place a `capture_devices` row comes into being.** The candidate must be `NEW` and hold a `REACHABLE` test that is still valid; the Core then verifies it once more with the credential of this request and, in one database transaction, writes the device, the credential when one is sent, and the audit rows. Any failure before or inside the transaction leaves nothing behind: there is no pending row.

**Web console only**, as operation 95 (`WEB_CONSOLE_SESSION`), and idle only (`409 CAPTURE_CONFIG_LOCKED`, no audit row).

**The target is the candidate in the path and nothing else** (R-9 AC-10): the Core takes the address from its own search state. A foreign id, an expired id and a candidate that is not testable are refused with 0 outbound requests. The adoption decides no track, no role and no address: assigning the new device to a video track is operation 78 or 79, which accept registered device ids only.

`credential` is the same pair as the body of operation 89 and must be present exactly when the passing test was authenticated: `422 INVALID_INPUT` with `details.reason` `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` or `CREDENTIAL_NOT_EXPECTED` otherwise. **The credential is write-only and lives for this one request** (C-N15; SEC35-34): it is not kept in the candidate state, not cached for a later request, and never written to a log line, an audit row, an error or a file. A retry is a new request with a newly sent credential. The answer says `credentialSet` and never echoes either field.

Other refusals, each storing nothing: `409 INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason` `CANDIDATE_ALREADY_REGISTERED` (plus `details.deviceId`; a repeat of an adoption answers this), `CANDIDATE_NOT_TESTED`, `CONNECTION_TEST_FAILED` (plus `details.outcome`, or `details.cause: DEVICE_CHANGED` when the device answers with other profiles than it did in the test) or `CONNECTION_TEST_IN_PROGRESS`.

Writes CAPTURE_CANDIDATE_ADOPTED, one CAPTURE_CONNECTION_TESTED row for the verification, and CAPTURE_CREDENTIAL_SET (the device id only) when a credential is stored. Publishes the `captureDevices` slice; `captureConfig` is not changed.

Over a bound the Core server answers `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `retry-after` and `details.reason` as operation 95: nothing is sent and no audit row is written. `503 NOT_READY` carries `details.reason` `CREDENTIAL_STORE_NOT_READY` when a credential is in the body and the Core credential store is not available, or `DISCOVERY_NOT_READY`. Both are envelope-level answers of the contract.

Simulated: the in-app simulator emulates this operation (OD-17 supersedes the old "simulator untouched" rule, OD-23); in Simulated mode a client calls it inside its own simulator. The simulator registers `CAM-03` for the first fixed candidate after a REACHABLE test, stores nothing of a credential and answers `credentialSet` as whether one was sent; a demo reset removes the device.

post.description:
Reads the local microphone inputs again and reports each **registered** microphone as present or not, with the named cause when a local input cannot be opened. **No body.** There is no network microphone discovery and no microphone adoption: the operation registers nothing and never replaces a local device by another one. Local inputs that are no registered microphone are counted only.

Needs CAPTURE_CONFIG, on the web console, a tablet or a phone, and is allowed while a session is open.

Writes one CAPTURE_DISCOVERY_SEARCHED row with `scope: MIC_LOCAL`. Publishes the `captureDevices` slice (`online` of the microphones).

Over a bound the Core server answers `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `retry-after` and `details.reason` `INPUT_RESCAN_RATE_LIMITED`: nothing is sent and no audit row is written. `503 NOT_READY` carries `details.reason` `CAPTURE_NOT_READY`. Both are envelope-level answers of the contract.

Simulated: the in-app simulator emulates this operation (OD-17 supersedes the old "simulator untouched" rule, OD-23); in Simulated mode a client calls it inside its own simulator. The simulator answers its two microphones, `present` from its device state.

CaptureConfigSlice.description: Slice `captureConfig`: the device selector (ops 76-80, 89). Its own slice, never the paired-client registry (E-04).

kind.description: The `capture_devices.kind` value set: CAMERA, MIC, POE.

host.description: Host or address only; never a credential URL (C-N8).

online.description: On a Core in its own capture this is the registry flag of the device (`capture_devices.enabled`), NOT a reachability reading: it is true from the moment the device is registered and changes only when a pre-check, a session start or a microphone re-scan has actually asked the source (false: it did not answer; true again: it answered). Outside those moments the Core has not checked the source, so `true` means "registered and not found unreachable at the last check" - never "reachable now": a client at rest says "Not checked", not "Online" or "Ready" (finding JW-23). In Simulated mode it is the demonstration model's value.

streamState.description: Null for a device with no stream (a mic, the PoE switch). Like `online`, not a reading at rest on a Core in its own capture (finding JW-23).

capabilities.description: Capability codes the adapters reported; an open set.

adapter.description: The adapter kind behind the device (C3 §2.6 "Device shapes"): `ONVIF_RTSP`, `USB_AUDIO`, `SNMP_POE`, `FAKE` or `LOCAL_DEVICE`. Present on a device that operation 96 registered.

sourceClass.description: Derived by the Core from `adapter`: `DEVELOPMENT` exactly for `FAKE` and `LOCAL_DEVICE`. Never set by a client.

sourceOpen.description: True while the Core holds this source open (C3 §2.6, erratum PE-128-38; SEC35-44 (4)): the "is on" fact of a `LOCAL_DEVICE` - the short open of a pre-check included. A runtime fact, never stored: absent when the source is not open, after a restart until it opens, and always in simulated capture.

items.description: One capture device (`dbc-3 §B.2`); carries no credential (RK-12).

dbfs.description: Ballistic level in dBFS; -90 means no signal.

noSignal.description: An input that should deliver samples delivers none (a fault word). Never set for a level that is simply not measured: see `notMeasured`.

notMeasured.description: Present and true when the Core does not measure this input now: no capture is open on a Core in its own capture. `dbfs` / `peak` then hold the floor as placeholders and `noSignal` is false; a client draws "Not measured" - no bars, no number, no "NO SIGNAL". Absent: the frame is a measured (or, on a simulated Core, generated) level.

additionalProperties.description: One 20 Hz audio frame: numbers and booleans only.

inputs.description: The newest frame of each of the two mic inputs of the capture, keyed by input ID `MIC-NN`: the built-in `MIC-01` / `MIC-02`, or the pair the selector holds (D133 (1)).

activeInputId.description: The input whose level is the one inside AUDIO-01 right now (op 81 moves it).

AudioSlice.description: Slice `audio`: the newest frame of each mic input plus the active one. Streamed in `meters` messages only; not part of a snapshot.

ReplicatedState.description: The 30 replicated slices of the Core state. No `auth`, `authLockout`, `pairing`, `clock` or `audio`, and no other member.

input.description: The create input after normalisation; `notes` is empty when none was given.

value.description: Live device state, e.g. ONLINE, READY, NO_SIGNAL, GNSS.

reason.description: Why the check warns or blocks (English fallback).

reasonCode.description: Machine-readable reason; null while pending or on PASS.

params.description: Values for the reason copy, e.g. `{ track: "AUDIO-01" }`.

sendingDeviceId.description: The paired device that sent this pre-check (fix wave I, D216): the audit row of its outcome names it. Absent: a web console session sent it.

etaMs.description: Estimated milliseconds left for this step.

detail.description: What the progress line shows (fragment count, chunk counters).

attempt.description: Attempt of this step, >= 1; a resumed run increments it.

label.description: English fallback; a client renders its own copy from `kind` and `params`.

coreNotRunning.description: Present on the restart fault of a Core in its own capture: the Core was not running while the session was active and does not know why. The kind stays `POWER_FAIL`; the fault is worded from this member, never as a power failure (closing pass J, D217 (5)). Absent: the fault is what its kind says.

fault.description: The critical fault that moved the session to FAULT, if any.

startTimeSource.description: Time source when the recording started.

stopTimeSource.description: Time source when the recording stopped or faulted.

captureConfig.description: Capture-config snapshot of this session (SH-06 writes it at start).

deviceId.description: The capture device feeding this track (`CAM-01`/`CAM-02`).

profile.description: Media profile code; an open set (OD-05/OD-06).

online.description: On a Core in its own capture this is the registry flag of the device (`capture_devices.enabled`), NOT a reachability reading: it is true from the moment the device is registered and changes only when a pre-check, a session start or a microphone re-scan has actually asked the source (false: it did not answer; true again: it answered). Outside those moments the Core has not checked the source, so `true` means "registered and not found unreachable at the last check" - never "reachable now": a client at rest says "Not checked", not "Online" or "Ready" (finding JW-23). In Simulated mode it is the demonstration model's value.

streamState.description: A lost stream is what makes a PoE cycle legal (OD-22). On a Core in its own capture the selector derives it from the same registry flag as `online` (`LIVE` for true, `LOST` for false): it is not a reading of a stream, and `LIVE` at rest does not say that the camera delivers pictures (finding JW-23).

items.description: One video slot of the device selector.

inputId.description: The mic input, `MIC-NN`: the built-in `MIC-01` / `MIC-02`, or a microphone registered later (D115 (2)).

deviceId.description: The microphone behind the input: the device of the same ID (D106 (4)).

online.description: On a Core in its own capture this is the registry flag of the device (`capture_devices.enabled`), NOT a reachability reading: it is true from the moment the device is registered and changes only when a pre-check, a session start or a microphone re-scan has actually asked the source (false: it did not answer; true again: it answered). Outside those moments the Core has not checked the source, so `true` means "registered and not found unreachable at the last check" - never "reachable now": a client at rest says "Not checked", not "Online" or "Ready" (finding JW-23). In Simulated mode it is the demonstration model's value.

items.description: One microphone slot of the device selector.

revision.description: Selector revision the snapshot was taken at.

audioSource.description: The active/standby mic pair of this session.

switchedAt.description: When the last switch took effect; null before the first.

intervalFromMs.description: Media-pts start of the interval the switch opened (never wall clock).

captureDurable.description: False from the accepted start until the first durable fragment ("connecting cameras"), then true; the state stays RECORDING (D84, D91 R-1). Absent reads as true.

captureCheckpoints.description: What the Core holds of a recording of its OWN capture: the fragment checkpoints the capture worker reported durable. Not stored; refreshed at most every 5 s and at the end of the capture. Absent in simulated capture, before the first checkpoint and on a session read back after a restart: absent means "not stated", never 0 (wave H Z1).

fragments.description: Durable fragment checkpoints of all camera files.

bytes.description: Stored bytes of the camera files the checkpoints cover (plaintext on the evidence volume until the seal).

lastAt.description: The Core clock at the newest checkpoint.

transcript.description: Transcript progress of the open session.

sha256.description: Null until the transcript is assembled and hashed.

ActiveSession.description: The open session with its pre-check, timeline, notes and finalization.

origin.description: Present on the one note of an EVIDENCE ITEM that carries the text of the session form's "Notes" field (`id: NOTE-FORM`, `at` = the creation of the session, `authorId` = who created it): written before the recording, copied onto the item when the item was made. Absent on a note written during the recording, and on every note of an open session.

SessionNote.description: A note an investigator wrote during the recording - or, on an evidence item, the session form's note (`origin`).

faultKind.description: INCOMPLETE only: the fault that ended it.

unsealableCause.description: Operation 38 only, on an INCOMPLETE entry that recorded and has no evidence item (its recordings are in the quarantine folder): the cause the Core recorded when it gave the seal up, as a code - `details.cause` of the audit row `SESSION_INCOMPLETE` (`details.reason: UNSEALABLE`) of that session, e.g. `SIGNING_KEY_UNAVAILABLE`. An open set. Read from the audit trail at each call, never reconstructed; absent when the trail holds no such row, on every other entry, and in the replicated `sessionHistory` slice (there the active alert of the session carries the same code: `params.cause` of the alert whose `target` is the session and whose `params.reason` is `UNSEALABLE`).

tracks.description: VIDEO-01, VIDEO-02, AUDIO-01 and AUDIO-02, each with its own hash. The two audio tracks are never merged.

value.description: sha256(manifestHash and keyId) for the simulated stand-in; the Ed25519 signature of the manifest hash for a real one.

algorithm.description: Schema v2: real seals sign with Ed25519 (OD-02); the stand-in remains for v1 rows.

developmentKey.description: Core server only: whether the certificate the SEALED manifest names is a development key - true / false as read from the item's own sealed manifest and certificate; null: could not be established (the package or its certificate is not readable). Absent: not stated (Simulated mode, a v1 item) - never to be read as a production key.

signature.description: The signature of the manifest: the simulated stand-in (v1) or a real Ed25519 (schema v2).

tampered.description: Set by the evidence tamper demo fault; verification then fails.

files.description: Schema v2: one whole file per camera (D224/D225) with its hashes; mirrors the simulator's `EvidenceFileEntry` (SH-07).

trackId.description: The track the file carries (VIDEO-01, VIDEO-02, AUDIO-01).

fileName.description: Relative path inside the package; never absolute or credential-bearing.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the whole file's stored bytes.

fragmentCount.description: Fragments the append-only file was written in (0 for the synthetic legacy shape).

sha256Plain.description: SHA-256 of the plaintext bytes (stored-bytes vs plaintext: both hashes verify).

fragmentChainHead.description: Head of this file's per-fragment hash chain (`dbc-3 §B.12`).

profile.description: Core server only, with `sealedPackage: PRESENT`: the SIGNED manifest's `tracks[].profile` of this file (manifest field 36), e.g. `H264_720P30` - the format the recorded stream declares, not the session's `profileId`. Absent: not stated (no sealed manifest was read).

fragmentChainHead.description: Schema v2 item-level chain head (SH-07 preview shape): the chain the fragments of this item continue.

transcriptSha256.description: Schema v2 item-level transcript hash (SH-07 preview; `evidence_items.transcript_sha256`, dbc-3 §B.11).

manifestVersion.description: Manifest version of the seal (`evidence_items.manifest_version`, dbc-3 §B.11): 2 for every v2 seal, also one without a transcript hash. Absent: derived as before.

labelsStatus.description: Whether the sealed transcript carries speaker labels (`evidence_items.labels_status`); null or absent when the seal states none.

developmentSources.description: Whether the seal recorded a development source (`evidence_items.development_sources`, manifest field 126; C3 §3.1 erratum PE-128-32). Null or absent: not recorded (a v1 item, or one sealed before the column existed) - never to be read as production.

audioSourceIntervals.description: Schema v2: which mic input fed AUDIO-01 over which media-pts spans (op 82 serves the full rows). On a Core, for a sealed item: the intervals of the SEALED manifest (`audio.sourceIntervals`, `seq` from 1), read from the item's own package.

toMs.description: Media-pts end; null for the open interval of a live session.

sourceClass.description: Wave H C1: the source class of the microphone of this interval as the sealed manifest records it (field 125). Absent: not stated.

sealedPackage.description: Core server only, for an item whose sealed v2 package lies in the Core's own store by its facts (a product seal, a seed-sealed demo item). PRESENT: its manifest was read from the package under the digest of record, and `files`, `audioSourceIntervals`, `interrupted` and `signature.developmentKey` are that manifest's. NOT_READABLE: the package is gone or its manifest is not the one the item was sealed with - no sealed fact is stated. Absent: the item has no package in the Core's store (a v1 demo item, a simulated item) - a client then shows nothing of a Core package.

interrupted.description: Core server only: the sealed manifest's `timeline.interrupted` - the package is the sealed durable prefix of a recording that did not end by a stop. Absent: not stated (no sealed manifest was read).

interruptedCause.description: Core server only, with `interrupted: true`: the code the item's custody entry `RECORDING_INTERRUPTED` names (a fault kind), or null when it names none.

streamProfileNotice.description: Core server only, operation 40: the session of this item carries the notice `STREAM_PROFILE_DIFFERS` (an alert of kind SYSTEM with that `params.reason`) - the recorded stream of the named tracks was not the configured profile, and the manifest states the stream. Present while the Core's alert list holds that notice. ABSENT: the Core holds no such notice for the session - never to be read as "compared and equal" for an item older than the alert list.

stream.description: What the recorded stream declared: the value the manifest states.

configured.description: What the selector had configured for the track.

transcriptModel.description: Core server only, for an item whose sealed v2 package lies in the Core's own store and whose SIGNED manifest declares a transcript document: the model of that transcript, from the manifest (decision D160). The same shape as `transcriptModel` of operation 41. For a server backend only the name exists, as reported by the STT server; version, quantisation and file hash are null and were not verified by the Core. Absent: not stated (no document sealed, a v1 or demonstration item, a package that could not be read, a manifest whose signature did not hold) - a reader draws nothing.

name.description: The model name the sealed manifest records.

version.description: The version the installation declared; null for a server backend.

quantisation.description: The quantisation read from the model file; null for a server backend.

modelSha256.description: SHA-256 of the model file as the Core hashed it; null for a server backend.

reportedByServer.description: True when the session's STT backend was a server: the name is what the server reported, and the Core verified nothing of the model.

report.description: The report line of the model, as operation 41 words it.

transcript.description: Schema v2: the transcript summary inside the item; the body arrives through op 84.

state.description: DISABLED only when R-8 turns STT off (D20; lands with M6).

sha256.description: Hash of the canonical transcript document; null until assembled.

machineTranscriptHash.description: Hash of the SEALED machine transcript — byte-unchanged by any revision (OD-15).

revision.description: Current max(revision_no); 0 when no revision exists (SEC35-21).

failedChunks.description: Chunks (not attempts) that ended FAILED; above 0 only with state PARTIAL. No text stands in for a failed chunk (D-EV-1; manifest field 93).

backendUnreachable.description: True when STT was enabled but the configured backend could not be reached for one or more chunks (manifest field 122).

EvidenceItem.description: One evidence item (schema v2 adds files, audio-source intervals and the transcript summary).

message.description: English fallback; a client renders its own copy from `type` and `params`.

SimEvent.description: One operational event. It never holds a password, a token, a code or a credential (SR-54).

kind.description: A fault kind, or SYSTEM for an alert no fault raised.

target.description: The fault target key, so clearing one target resolves its alert.

actorId.description: Operator ID, or null for the system. Never a username typed at a failed sign-in.

message.description: English fallback; a client renders its own copy from `type` and `details`.

deviceId.description: A device of the Core (e.g. CAM-01) or a paired device of the registry (`DEV-NNNN`), or null.

details.description: Flat values. Never a password, a token, a code, a credential or a typed username (SR-54).

hash.description: sha256(prevHash and the canonical JSON of the twelve members above).

AuditRow.description: One audit row with its full hashed body, so a client can verify the chain itself.

connectionId.description: Names this socket in the server's log. Not a credential.

epoch.description: The epoch of the Core state when the connection opened.

principal.description: Who the server took this connection for, from the upgrade request's headers only.

reason.description: Only with ANONYMOUS: the connection presented a credential the server did not accept.

topics.description: The topics this connection is given. Always `heartbeat`; never more than the principal's set.

serverTime.description: Epoch milliseconds on the server clock.

RealtimeHello.description: First message of every connection: who the server took the caller for, and what it will send.

RealtimeSnapshot.description: The whole replicated state: after `hello`, as the answer to `resync`, and when a new epoch starts.

head.description: Hash of the newest row after the append.

total.description: Rows ever appended, after the append.

dropped.description: Rows dropped off the front of the ring, after the append.

RealtimeDeltaOp.description: One operation of a delta: `replace` one whole slice, or `append` rows to `audit` or `events`.

revision.description: Exactly the previous revision plus 1 within the epoch. Revisions are gap-free.

ops.description: Applied in order. A slice no op names is not touched.

RealtimeDelta.description: One change of the replicated state. State deltas are never dropped.

seq.description: Counts the frames the server produced; a skipped frame leaves a gap, by design. It never goes back on a connection, also across a new epoch.

RealtimeMeters.description: One meter frame of both mic inputs, with the active one (SH-17). Sent only after `subscribe`; it carries no revision, and the latest value wins.

operator.description: The operator of the session: ID and new role, nothing else.

permissions.description: The permissions of the new role. A display hint: the server decides every call.

RealtimeSessionUpdated.description: The role of the session's operator changed. The session stays; nobody is signed out.

RealtimeSessionEnded.description: The session of this socket ended. The server closes the connection with 4401 right after.

RealtimeDeviceRevoked.description: The device of this socket is no longer paired. The server closes the connection with 4403 right after.

RealtimeAdminChanged.description: A list of an administration page changed. It names the list only; the client refetches it through REST.

oneOf.description: Start the `meters` frames on this connection.
Stop the `meters` frames on this connection.
Ask for a new `snapshot` after a revision gap or another epoch. At most one in 2 s; one that comes sooner is answered when the 2 s have passed.

RealtimeClientMessage.description: A message a client sends on `/ws`. Anything else closes the connection with 1008; a message larger than 65,536 bytes closes it with 1009.

label.description: Label of the marker: at most 80 UTF-16 code units after trimming. Omitted or empty: the Core names it "Marker n".

text.description: The note: 1 to 2,000 characters after trimming, and at most 2,000 UTF-16 code units. It stays in the session record; the audit row holds its ID and length only.

caseNumber.description: The next case number `LP/{YYYY}/{MMDD}-NNNN`. It is reserved: the next scan offers another.

CaseNumberScan.description: Result of the simulated case-number scanner.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

PageQuery.description: Query of a list read that takes no filter: the paging members of API-9.

items.description: Finished sessions, newest first: the elements of the `sessionHistory` slice.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

SessionHistoryPage.description: One page of the session history.

caseType.description: Only items of this case type (the subject type of the session).

q.description: Search text, 1 to 100 characters after trimming: matched without regard to case against the evidence ID, the session ID, the case number and the subject name.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

EvidenceListQuery.description: Query of `GET /api/v1/evidence`: filters, a search text and the paging members of API-9.

items.description: Evidence items, newest recording first: the elements of the `evidence` slice.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

source.description: DEMO_PACKAGE: the demo package a client bundles belongs to this item. LIVE_STREAM (schema v2): a signed media session (op 88) can play the decrypted camera file. NONE: no media exists for it.

packageSuffix.description: The join key of the bundled package, e.g. `0004`; null when the source is not DEMO_PACKAGE.

fileIds.description: Core server only, with LIVE_STREAM: the camera files the sealed package of the item really holds (one or two), in file order - the `fileId` values operation 88 accepts for it.

reason.description: Core server only, with NONE: why no media can be played, as a code. `NOT_SEALED` (the item was never sealed: an interrupted or unsealable recording), `NOT_A_SEALED_PACKAGE` (no sealed package of this item lies in the Core's store and no bundled demo package belongs to it), `DEMONSTRATION_RECORD` (fix wave J: the item is the record of a session of a Core in SIMULATED capture - a demonstration that recorded no media; a client says so and never "no sealed package in the evidence store"), or a code of the package itself: `PACKAGE_MISSING` (the folder is gone, e.g. quarantined), `MANIFEST_UNREADABLE`, `MANIFEST_NOT_OF_ITEM`, `CAMERA_FILE_MISSING`, `CAMERA_FILE_SIZE_MISMATCH`, `FRAGMENT_TABLE_INVALID`, `FRAGMENT_TOO_LARGE`, `SESSION_KEY_UNAVAILABLE`. An open set.

EvidenceMediaRef.description: Which media belongs to an evidence item. It names no file and no path: playback travels through the signed media session of operation 88 (E-31; the v1 MS-1 reading stays true for Simulated mode).

access.description: Core server only: what THIS caller may do with the item, so that a page view asks for nothing it would be refused (a refusal is an audited row).

play.description: This caller may open a media session for the item (operation 88): false for REAL evidence the caller does not hold (SEC35-16). A client that reads false does not ask.

readTranscript.description: This caller is inside the case scope the transcript operations (84, 86) hold for the item.

export.description: This caller has EVIDENCE_EXPORT and is inside the case scope of the item (operations 42, 87 and the download).

exports.description: Core server only, and only for a caller with `access.export`: the finished exports of the item whose archive lies in the Core's store, newest first. Each can be downloaded again through operation 87 by its `jobId`. Archives are kept until the package is removed; none is deleted by the product.

jobId.description: `EXPJ-NNNNNN`: the `{id}` of operation 87, which answers a fresh signed download path for it.

exportedBy.description: The operator ID the signed export manifest names (`export.exportedBy`).

archiveBytes.description: The length of the archive file as it lies on the Core.

archiveSha256.description: SHA-256 of the archive file, when the Core has computed it in this run; operation 87 always answers it (`archive.sha256`).

items.description: One finished export of an evidence item: the archive lies in the Core's store.

exportDestinationDefault.description: Core server only: the destination text the Core records for an export request that names none - `Case file transfer` on a Core in its own capture, `Case file transfer (simulated)` on a Core in simulated capture. A client pre-selects the destination whose recorded text equals it, so that every client offers the same default.

exportKinds.description: Core server only: the export outputs of operation 42 and whether this Core can produce each. A client offers a kind ENABLED only when its entry says `available: true`, and draws an unavailable kind disabled with its reason. Absent (Simulated mode, an older Core): only PACKAGE is offered.

available.description: True: a request of this kind is accepted. False: it is refused (`409 COMMAND_UNSUPPORTED`) before any job.

reason.description: Present exactly when `available` is false: why, as a code - `COMPOSITE_ENCODER_NOT_SELECTED` (no encoder is selected in this build).

EvidenceDetail.description: One evidence item and the reference to its media.

ok.description: True when every file, the transcript hash, the manifest and the signature verify.

at.description: When the verification ran, on the server clock.

expected.description: The sealed hash of the track.

tracks.description: One result per v1 track; a schema-v2 item answers `files` instead (C3 §3 op 41).

files.description: Schema v2: one result per camera file, both hashes and the fragment chain.

storedOk.description: Hash of the stored bytes matches the sealed value.

plainOk.description: Hash of the plaintext bytes matches the sealed value.

plainChecked.description: Present and false when the plaintext check (V-05) did not run for this file: `plainOk: false` is then "not checked", not a failed comparison. Absent: `plainOk` is the result of the check.

chainOk.description: Every fragment checkpoint continues the chain (V-11 idiom; one tampered fragment answers false — OD-02 L2).

transcriptOk.description: Schema v2: the sealed transcript hash matches the stored document; absent for an item without a transcript.

signatureOk.description: Schema v2: a real Ed25519 signature is verified with the Core public key (OD-02).

demonstration.description: Present and true on every verdict the SIMULATOR computed (a `SIMULATED` item, a v1 `DEMO_PACKAGE` item): the hashes of a demonstration record were compared and no stored media was read. A client words such a verdict as a demonstration, never as a bare "verified by the Core". Absent on the verdict of a real sealed package.

overall.description: Schema v2: PASS, or the gravest failure class among the findings.

interrupted.description: Schema v2: the package is the sealed durable prefix of an interrupted recording (V-12). A state, not a failure.

checks.description: Schema v2: the per-check report, V-01 to V-15 in order, so that a client can name the check that failed.

failureClass.description: The class of the first finding; null unless the status is FAIL.

file.description: A path inside the package, `/` separated; never a host path.

member.description: A dotted member path of the manifest.

findings.description: WHERE the check found something: names, never a value of the package.

findingCount.description: How many findings the check has when `findings` was cut; absent when it lists them all.

fragments.description: Schema v2: the fragments that did not verify, over both camera files (V-08 names the fragment). Fragments that verified are counted in `files`, not listed.

storedOk.description: The stored bytes of the fragment hash to the sealed value (V-04).

plainOk.description: The decrypted fragment hashes to the sealed value (V-05); null: not checked.

failedFragmentCount.description: Schema v2: how many fragments did not verify; larger than `fragments.length` when the list was cut.

transcriptState.description: Schema v2: what the verified package says of its transcript (seven codes; D110).

report.description: The English report line of the state; a client words the state by `code`.

transcriptModel.description: Schema v2 (decision D160): the model of the sealed transcript, from the signed manifest. For a server backend only the name exists, as reported by the STT server; version, quantisation and file hash are null and were not verified by the Core. Absent when no transcript document is sealed, for a v1 item, and when the manifest is not the signed one.

name.description: The model name the sealed manifest records.

version.description: The version the installation declared; null for a server backend.

quantisation.description: The quantisation read from the model file; null for a server backend.

modelSha256.description: SHA-256 of the model file as the Core hashed it; null for a server backend.

reportedByServer.description: True when the session's STT backend was a server: the name is what the server reported, and the Core verified nothing of the model.

report.description: The report line of the model.

sources.description: Schema v2 (V-15; R-11): the source class of every recorded source. A development package verifies with `ok: true` at the top level and `sources.code: DEVELOPMENT`; the value of the mark never changes the verdict. Absent for a v1 item: its source class is not recorded, which is never read as production.

ok.description: V-15 passed: the mark is present, well-formed and consistent. It says nothing of the value of the mark.

code.description: DEVELOPMENT: at least one source is LOCAL_DEVICE or FAKE (not a failure). DECLARED_PRODUCTION: every source reads PRODUCTION - a statement of the Core that sealed the package, not a fact the verifier proved. NOT_TRUSTWORTHY: the manifest is not the signed one or its mark is missing or inconsistent; no class is stated. UNKNOWN: no readable v2 manifest.

development.description: Recomputed by the verifier from the classes. null exactly when `code` is NOT_TRUSTWORTHY or UNKNOWN: nothing is stated, and null is never read as production.

report.description: The English source line, the first line of a verify report; a client words the state by `code`.

tracks.description: Manifest field 124 of each camera file; empty when nothing is stated.

audioIntervals.description: Manifest field 125 of each interval of the session audio track; empty when nothing is stated.

signature.description: Schema v2 (decisions D147, D178): what the verified package says of its signing KEY. developmentKey.description: True when the subject of the certificate that VERIFIED the signature carries the development-key mark (`OU=DEVELOPMENT KEY - NOT FOR PRODUCTION`); false when it does not. `null`: NOT ESTABLISHED - the manifest, the signature or the certificate did not verify (never `false` from an unverified package). code.description: `AUDIT_EXTRACT_NOT_SIGNED` (every v2 result): `audit-session-extract.jsonl` is in the package and its content is covered by no hash and no signature. `EXPORT_FOLDER_UNEXPECTED_FILE` (only when there is such a file): the `export/` folder of the package holds a file that is no finished export - a `.partial` a stopped export left, a name no export writes, or anything in a sub-folder; the sealed set is not affected. `REVISION_APPEND_PENDING` (only while there is such a file): a transcript revision is being written - `transcript/transcript-revisions.json.next` lies in the package; it fails nothing; verify again shortly.

baseRevision.description: The item's CURRENT max(revision_no) as the caller saw it (0 when none). A mismatch answers 409 TRANSCRIPT_REVISION_CONFLICT; the check runs inside the minting transaction (SEC35-21; dbc-3 §B.9).

Outside those moments the Core has not checked the source, so `true` means "registered and not found unreachable at the last check" - never "reachable now": a client at rest says "Not checked", not "Online" or "Ready" (finding JW-23). In Simulated mode it is the demonstration model's value.

streamState.description: Null for a device with no stream (a mic, the PoE switch). Like `online`, not a reading at rest on a Core in its own capture (finding JW-23).

capabilities.description: Capability codes the adapters reported; an open set.

adapter.description: The adapter kind behind the device (C3 §2.6 "Device shapes"): `ONVIF_RTSP`, `USB_AUDIO`, `SNMP_POE`, `FAKE` or `LOCAL_DEVICE`. Present on a device that operation 96 registered.

sourceClass.description: Derived by the Core from `adapter`: `DEVELOPMENT` exactly for `FAKE` and `LOCAL_DEVICE`. Never set by a client.

sourceOpen.description: True while the Core holds this source open (C3 §2.6, erratum PE-128-38; SEC35-44 (4)): the "is on" fact of a `LOCAL_DEVICE` - the short open of a pre-check included. A runtime fact, never stored: absent when the source is not open, after a restart until it opens, and always in simulated capture.

device.description: One capture device (`dbc-3 §B.2`); carries no credential (RK-12).

credentialSet.description: Whether a credential was stored with the device: a fact, never a value.

CaptureCandidateAdoption.description: The capture device an adoption registered (C3 §2.6 op 96).

inputId.description: The mic input (`MIC-NN`) this device stands behind in the selector; null when it is assigned to none.

adapter.description: The adapter kind of the microphone. ABSENT on a Core in SIMULATED capture, which states no adapter and no source class on any operation (decision D196, gate 70 finding G70-01).

sourceClass.description: Derived by the Core from `adapter`; absent exactly when `adapter` is.

errorCode.description: The named cause when a local input cannot be opened; null otherwise.

unregisteredCount.description: Local inputs that are no registered microphone: a count only.

CaptureInputScan.description: The local microphone inputs as a re-read found them (C3 §2.6 op 97). It registers nothing.

XRequestId.description: The ID of the request in the Core server's log. An error envelope repeats it as `error.requestId`.

XDemsEpoch.description: The epoch of the Core state: it counts demo resets and scenario loads. An integer, sent as decimal text (API-7).

XDemsRevision.description: The revision of the delta that holds the command's effect (the current revision when nothing replicated changed). An integer, sent as decimal text; it restarts at 0 with each epoch (API-7).

RetryAfter.description: Whole seconds until the caller's key is counted afresh.

InvalidPath.description: 400 INVALID_PATH. The path is malformed, or a path parameter is not valid percent-encoding.

NotFound.description: 404 NOT_FOUND. No operation has this path.

MethodNotAllowed.description: 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED. The path exists, but not with this method.

NotReady.description: 503 NOT_READY. The database or the engine is not ready, or a demo reset is running. Every operation except health.

OriginNotAllowed.description: 403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED. The `Origin` header is not on the list that fits the credential the request carries (01_specs §14.2).

CredentialConflict.description: 401 NOT_SIGNED_IN (`details.reason: CREDENTIAL_CONFLICT`). The request carries a session cookie and an `Authorization` header: one credential per request (ID-12).

RateLimited.description: 429 RATE_LIMITED. The request throttle, or the denial budget of the caller's key (20 audited refusals in 60 s), is used up.

PayloadTooLarge.description: 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE. The request body is larger than 65,536 bytes.

InvalidJson.description: 400 INVALID_JSON. A body was sent that is not a JSON object. Every POST, also one that takes no body; an empty body is no body.

InternalError.description: 500 INTERNAL_ERROR or SIMULATOR_ERROR. An unexpected failure; the answer holds no detail. SIMULATOR_ERROR is the in-app simulator's code.

sessionCookie.name: dems_session_4420
sessionCookie.description: The session of a web console. `signIn` sets it as an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie without an expiry, and its body then holds no token; the browser attaches the cookie to same-origin requests and to the socket upgrade. The name is `dems_session_<listen port>`: `dems_session_4420` on the main instance. It resolves only a session that is not bound to a device, and a POST that carries it must come from a web console origin.

bearerAuth.description: A paired device. `Authorization: Bearer` carries the device credential (prefix `dvc_`) on the device operations and at sign-in, and the session token (prefix `ses_`) once an operator is signed in on the device. The server stores only a hash of either. One credential per request: a request that carries the session cookie and this header is refused. Neither value ever travels in a URL.
